name: Paged, indexed delta stream of agent state
what: The conversation view receives only changed steps and side collections (artifacts, file diffs, background tasks, queued input, pending agent messages) instead of re-fetching a transcript; older steps load on scroll.
how: LanguageServerService.StreamAgentStateUpdates (server stream) takes conversation_id, subscriber_id, initial Slice page bounds for steps/generator/executor metadata, a ClientTrajectoryVerbosity (DEBUG, PROD_UI, FULL), disable_rehydration and enable_latency_telemetry. Each AgentStateUpdate carries indices + total_length + page_bounds per collection (StepsUpdate, QueuedStepsUpdate, ArtifactSnapshotsUpdate, TrajectoryFileDiffsUpdate, BackgroundTasksUpdate, PendingAgentMessagesUpdate, AccumulatedSectionsUpdate) plus subtrajectory updates for subagents. RequestAgentStatePageUpdate fetches more pages. The UI shows a load-older control.
verevonRelevance: Verevon streams a flat SSE event taxonomy and re-derives nodes client-side (baseline s1, s13); a slice/index delta contract per collection would fix full-message reparsing and give resume-by-page for session-core runs.
notes: Quality 5: explicit paging, verbosity tiers, per-subscriber state, rehydration switch. Decoded from the descriptors embedded in language_server.exe, not from docs. Peer streams (Codex app-server items, AG-UI) are event-based; per-collection slice paging with verbosity tiers was not seen in the sibling inventories.

name: Server-driven step render hints
what: Tool and MCP steps can ship their own title, file references, markdown, icon, aggregation key, progress and media blocks so the UI renders them without a per-tool component.
how: StepRenderInfo (title, title_prefix, markdown, hidden, icon, aggregation_key, StepProgress, TitlePart with FileRef{uri,start_line,end_line}, ContentBlock markdown|MediaRef). Used by CortexStepMcpTool.render_info, CortexStepSystemMessage and CortexStepGeneric/GenericStepResult. The UI also has fixed past/present-tense labels for built-in steps (searched web, ran command, invoked subagent, generated image, used MCP tool).
verevonRelevance: Lets Model Plane plugins and MCP tools (currently registered but not executable, baseline s5) render rich cards through a typed render_info field rather than new SPA components.

name: Queue or interrupt: message delivery strategy
what: A follow-up typed while the agent runs can either interrupt immediately or wait until the current turn ends; the choice is a global setting and a per-message toggle, and queued messages can be deleted before delivery.
how: MessageDeliveryStrategy enum (NEXT_INVOCATION, WHEN_IDLE) on SendUserCascadeMessageRequest and AgentMessage; UserSettings.queued_message_delivery_strategy; QueuedStepsUpdate and DeleteQueuedUserInputStep RPC; composer copy distinguishes Send immediately from Queue message and tags sends-on-next-turn vs sends-after-finish.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already queues mid-run input (baseline s1 "Mid-run messages") but only as in-memory single-replica state; the next-invocation vs when-idle distinction and an explicit interrupt option are cheap UX gains.

name: Fork a conversation at any step
what: The user can fork a conversation from a chosen step into a new conversation, optionally in a different workspace, and view the fork in a split pane.
how: ForkConversationRequest {source_cascade_id, fork_at_step_index, target_fork_workspace, source_workspace_uris, items, media, agent_script_override, reference_type}; CortexTrajectoryReferenceType values FORK, PRUNE, THOUGHT_REWRITE, BATTLE_MODE, SUBAGENT_FORK; metadata keeps parent/root conversation ids; UI has Fork Conversation, fork-in-current-workspace and close-split-and-go-to-fork actions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon "Branch" is browser-only until it sends and there is no server branching (baseline s1, known gap 8); a server-owned fork-at-step with reference type would close it in session-core.
notes: THOUGHT_REWRITE reference type hints at editing prior reasoning; semantics not verified.

name: Turn-level undo with diff preview
what: The user can revert the workspace to the state before any earlier turn; a preview lists the per-file diffs that would be undone, with warnings when the agent made no edits or the workspace changed independently.
how: GetRevertPreview returns CodeEditRevertPreview{file_uri, UnifiedDiff, action_type}; RevertToCascadeStep restores to step_index using SnapshotMetadata taken per user step (UserStepSnapshot, RecordUserStepSnapshot); executor flag cortex_snapshot_revert; UI disables revert before a Best-of-N trigger point and for turns carrying artifact, file or diff comments.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no checkpoint or rewind (baseline s4, planned I11); previewed revert per user step is the reference design, though Verevon effects are provider actions rather than files so the preview would be a receipt list.
notes: Works because the agent edits a local working tree that can be snapshotted; effectful provider actions (Verevon) are not reversible this way.

name: Conversation organisation and annotations
what: Conversations can be pinned, starred, archived, marked unread, titled, tagged and grouped; the sidebar groups by workspace or project, sorts by last updated, last prompt or date added, and filters (pinned only, unread only, last 7 days, scheduled, extensions).
how: ConversationAnnotations {title, tags, archived, starred, last_user_view_time, marked_as_unread, group_id/index/description, pinned, cls, active_profile, conversation_group_id}; UpdateConversationAnnotations RPC; a public-shaped product API ConversationService (Create/List/Get/Update/Delete with project_id, parent id, tags, include_archived, paging); keyboard actions mark read/unread, archive, delete.
verevonRelevance: Verevon projects/folders are a browser-only organiser capped at 100 with a thread list capped at 80 (baseline s1); persisting annotations server-side in session-core would make organisation cross-device.

name: Conversation picker, search and in-thread find
what: A keyboard picker switches conversations and searches all of them; the agent can also search its own past conversations; in-thread find has case, word and regex toggles.
how: Ctrl+K picker and Ctrl+Shift+K workspace selector; SearchConversations RPC {query, limit}; TRAJECTORY_SEARCH step with TrajectorySearchToolConfig (conversations_enabled, user_activities_enabled, max_scored_chunks) lets the model retrieve chunks from other trajectories; Ctrl+F find-in-conversation with match-case/whole-word/regex controls.
verevonRelevance: Verevon search is substring over the loaded thread titles with no recall tool (baseline s1, s8); a trajectory-search tool over session-core threads is the matching agent-facing feature.

name: Shareable conversation links and Markdown export
what: A conversation can be shared by link (viewers load a read-only copy) or exported to Markdown; admins can block sharing.
how: CreateTrajectoryShare (status TEAM) / FetchTrajectoryShare / DeleteTrajectoryShare on ApiServer, LoadSharedTrajectory in the LS, deep link import path in the UI, ConvertTrajectoryToMarkdown; PlanInfo.can_share_conversations and IsConversationSharingBlocked gate it. The share dialog warns that history is exported.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has neither share links nor export of a thread to Markdown (baseline s1 absent); sharing must respect ZDR and Space ACL rules, so a signed, org-scoped read-only snapshot is the safe shape.
notes: Sharing uploads the full trajectory to Google servers; contrast with ZDR constraints in Verevon.

name: Markdown, math and diagram rendering stack
what: Agent replies render GitHub-flavoured Markdown with KaTeX math (the prompt invites math only when the planner config flags LaTeX support), syntax highlighting, foldable code blocks, copy/insert-in-terminal actions and Mermaid diagrams laid out with ELK.
how: UI bundle includes react-markdown, remark-gfm, remark-math, rehype-raw, rehype-sanitize, rehype-slug, katex and a Prism bundle; planner config supports_latex_rendering controls the prompt; diagrams use an injected Mermaid component with the ELK layout engine; code blocks offer fold/unfold, copy, at-mention and insert-in-terminal; images are blocked in strict mode.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already ships KaTeX, Mermaid and charts (baseline s1); the useful extras are per-model LaTeX gating and sanitised raw HTML via rehype-sanitize.
notes: Library list read from the Package licence comments in the Closure-compiled main.js.

name: Rich composer with typed scope items and inline slash tokens
what: The prompt box is a rich editor where @-mentions (files, code items, web pages, conversations, MCP resources/prompts) and slash commands become typed inline tokens; drafts persist per conversation.
how: Lexical editor (typeahead menu, mention nodes, autosize); text is serialised to TextOrScopeItem chunks (text or scope item) in SendUserCascadeMessageRequest.items; slash commands come from GetSlashCommands (SlashCommandType SYSTEM or SKILL, with arguments); MCP prompts fetched via GetMcpPrompt; draftsRef keyed per conversation; welcome chips insert prefilled slash-command tokens.
verevonRelevance: Verevon composer is a 5,925-line component with a plain slash menu (baseline s5, s12); typed scope items give the model structured references instead of pasted text.

name: Ask-the-user structured questions and suggested replies
what: The agent can pause to ask one or more questions with selectable options, multi-select or free-text, which the user can skip; it can also offer suggested replies.
how: CortexStepAskQuestion / AskQuestionEntry {question, options, is_multi_select, selected_option_ids, write_in_response, skipped}; interaction spec/response messages (AskQuestionInteraction with cancelled); AskQuestionToolConfig; SUGGESTED_RESPONSES step; UI has previous/next question navigation and OS notifications that the agent has questions. Planning prompt tells the model to put open questions inside the plan rather than use the tool.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approvals are binary cards (baseline s4); a typed multi-question interaction is a small contract that lets the Do loop clarify requirements without free-text round trips.

name: Side questions without interrupting the run
what: The user can ask an out-of-band question in a resizable side panel while the main agent keeps working; the answer is dismissible and kept out of the main thread.
how: CORTEX_TRAJECTORY_TYPE_SIDE_QUESTION; UI sideQuestionFeature, panel resize/dismiss controls, side question text prepended in prompts; public docs describe /btw as a background-thread question that does not pause the main agent.
verevonRelevance: Maps to a second lightweight run on the same thread; Verevon could implement it as a read-only ask-loop turn tagged side_question so it never enters the Do run history.
notes: Claude Code has a similar /btw command, so uncommon rather than unique.

name: Artifact viewer with selection comments and export
what: Artifacts (plans, walkthroughs, task lists, images, recordings) open in an auxiliary pane; users select text or image regions and attach comments, copy images, or export the artifact.
how: ArtifactSnapshot {name, uri, last_edited, ArtifactReviewState, ArtifactMetadata, content | UrlArtifactPayload}; ArtifactMetadata {artifact_type IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN|WALKTHROUGH|TASK|OTHER, summary, version, request_feedback, user_facing}; ArtifactComment targets full file or selections (ArtifactSelectionTarget, ArtifactImageSelection); aux pane views include Artifact Viewer, Global Artifact Viewer, File Viewer, Browser Subagent Viewer.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has an artifact panel with version stepper and diff but no editor or commenting (baseline s1 "Editing artifacts by hand" absent); selection comments that flow back to the model are the missing half.
notes: Quality 5: comments are first-class inputs to the next agent turn, not chat text.

name: Collapsible reasoning and verbose chat mode
what: Intermediate thinking is shown as a collapsible "thought" with duration; a Verbose Agent Chat setting keeps intermediate thinking steps visible; conversation width is adjustable.
how: CortexStepPlannerResponse carries thinking, raw_thinking, thinking_duration, signature, thinking_redacted; UserSettings.verbose_agent_chat; ConversationWidth DEFAULT/NARROW/WIDE; ui strings Thinking for / Thought Process / Copy thinking.
verevonRelevance: Verevon streams reasoning_delta into a collapsible trace (baseline s9); the persisted thinking_duration and redaction flag are details worth keeping on the step record.

name: Single web bundle served by the local Go server
what: The whole chat/agent UI is one single-page web app (React, Redux Toolkit, Lexical, xterm.js, KaTeX, ELK) served by the local Go server into an Electron window; the same bundle serves Remote Control in a browser and an installable PWA.
how: index.html titled Jetski Web with viewport and process polyfills; main.js (8.9 MB Closure-compiled) plus compiled Tailwind CSS, jetbox.css, prism_bundle.js, an AudioWorklet and a diff worker are embedded as a zip inside language_server.exe (zip entries recovered by local-file-header scan) and served over HTTPS on 127.0.0.1; PWA/notification strings for installing the site as an app.
verevonRelevance: Confirms a single-bundle UI that works both in a desktop shell and a remote browser; Verevon is web-first already, so the relevant lesson is the installable-PWA plus push path for long runs.
notes: REA analyze_javascript_application on the extracted UI directory parsed 4 JS files (1.58M AST nodes) but exhausted its heap on main.js semantic analysis, so feature tracing used direct source reads.

name: Attachment pipeline gated by model capability
what: Images, PDFs, text/CSV/JSON/Markdown, audio and video can be attached by drag and drop, paste or picker; the send button refuses media the selected model cannot take.
how: Limits enforced client-side (PDF up to 10 MB, text up to 1 MB, a maximum attachment count, three upload retries, video at least one second); Media {mime_type, inline_data|blobref, uri, thumbnail, duration}; ModelFeatures supports_images/pdf/video plus supported_mime_types per ClientModelConfig; WRITE_BLOB step stores bytes; drop target says Drop to add to Agent.
verevonRelevance: Verevon attachments are capped at 1 MB and text-extracted (baseline s2); a per-model mime-type capability table prevents silent stripping on the ChatGPT-subscription route.

name: Streaming voice dictation with cleanup
what: A microphone button or Ctrl+M streams speech into the composer (and into artifact comments); after recording, filler words and self-corrections are cleaned into one prompt using conversation context.
how: AudioWorklet downsamples to 16 kHz PCM and posts 40 ms chunks; LS RPCs StreamAudioTranscription / SendAudioChunk / EndAudioSession and a batch GetTranscription; UI shows finalizing-transcription state and blocks recording while the Concierge mic is on; cleanup behaviour is from public docs.
verevonRelevance: Verevon dictation is one governed call per utterance with no streaming (baseline s2); chunked streaming plus a post-edit pass is the upgrade without needing duplex voice.
notes: The post-recording cleanup is DOC-only; the binary shows the transcription streaming path.

name: Image generation and editing tool
what: The agent can generate or edit images (UI mockups, diagrams, app assets) from a prompt and reference images, and saves them as artifacts.
how: CortexStepGenerateImage {prompt, image_paths for edit/combine, image_name, aspect_ratio, generated_image/media, model_name}; GenerateImageToolConfig {output_directory}; GetImageGeneration RPC on ApiServer; public docs name a dedicated non-selectable image model.
verevonRelevance: Verevon image mode exists but no image editing (baseline s2, known gap 8); accepting image_paths for edit/combine is a small contract change.

name: Screen and video attachments analysed by the agent
what: Users can attach a screen recording or video; the UI states the agent is analysing videos and rejects clips shorter than a second.
how: UI MediaRecorder/getUserMedia paths, Screen Recording and Failed to start screen recording strings; Media.duration_seconds; StartScreenRecording/SaveScreenRecording/HandleScreenRecording RPCs; model gating through ModelFeatures.supports_video.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has one-shot screenshot attach only and no video understanding (baseline s2); video as a typed Media part is the shape to copy if a Gemini route is added.
notes: Relies on string and RPC names; end-to-end behaviour not exercised.

name: Jupyter notebook read, edit and execute tools
what: The agent can read, edit and run cells of .ipynb files, restarting the kernel and receiving text and image outputs.
how: CortexStepReadNotebook / EditNotebook (insert before/after, replace, delete, overwrite) / ExecuteNotebook {cell ids/indices, stop_on_error, restart_kernel, use_message_bridge} with per-cell status, truncated output, generated images and blobs; NotebookEditToolConfig; extension-server bridge RPCs.
verevonRelevance: Verevon data analysis is a networkless 30 s code_interpreter with no persisted cells (baseline s2); a stateful notebook object with per-cell outputs is the durable alternative.
notes: Requires an IDE/notebook host bridge; in the Hub it relies on the LS extension bridge.

name: Google Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides links as context
what: Pasted Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides links resolve to titled chips; if access is denied the link stays as plain text.
how: UI strings for Drive/Docs/Sheets/Slides icons and title-resolution timeouts; SearchDriveFiles RPC; connector enums for GOOGLE_DRIVE in the knowledge-base proto (scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Verevon has connector pickers for Drive/Outlook/Gmail (baseline s2); title-resolving inline chips that degrade to text on 403 are a nice detail.

name: Web search and chunked page reading with permission gate
what: The agent can search the web (text or image), read a URL (asking permission first when the URL is not allowlisted) and read long pages in chunks with an outline.
how: CortexStepSearchWeb {query, domain, web_documents, summary, third_party_config (Gemini grounding), SearchWebType WEB|IMAGE}; CortexStepReadUrlContent {url, resolved_url, latency_ms, user_rejected, content_path}; VIEW_CONTENT_CHUNK; CascadeReadUrlContentInteraction; UI shows reading page, created outline, page was short enough to be read as a single document.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has web_search/fetch_url and deep research (baseline s3); the outline-then-chunk read and the explicit read permission step are details for long documents.

name: Knowledge Items distilled automatically from conversations
what: The system generates reusable Knowledge Items (title, summary, references to files, conversations or URLs) from past work and inserts relevant ones into later runs.
how: KnowledgeConfig {enabled, model, max_context_tokens, max_invocations, min_turns_between_knowledge_generation, max_knowledge_items, max_artifacts_per_ki, max_title/summary_length, enable_ki_insertion}; steps KNOWLEDGE_GENERATION, KI_INSERTION, KNOWLEDGE_ARTIFACTS; trajectory type KNOWLEDGE_GENERATION; a tool schema asks for title, one-paragraph summary and references; KnowledgeReference supports file, conversation id or url.
verevonRelevance: Comparable to Verevon "Dreaming" memory extraction in session-core (baseline s8); the explicit cadence limits (min turns between generations, max items) are a good guardrail.
notes: UI and docs barely mention Knowledge Items; they live under the app data brain directory.

what: A knowledge-base search tool can query connected GitHub, Google Drive, Jira, Slack and email corpora with time ranges, and the plan flag knowledge_base_enabled gates it.
how: CortexStepSearchKnowledgeBase {queries, time_range, connector_types, aggregate_ids, knowledge_base_groups}; CortexStepLookupKnowledgeBase / ReadKnowledgeBaseItem; PlanInfo.knowledge_base_enabled; KnowledgeBaseService RPCs for ingestion and webhooks in the opensearch_clients proto (scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Verevon owns this in Data Plane v2 and integration-corev2; nothing to copy beyond a connector_types filter on the retrieval tool.
notes: Availability in the shipped 2.0 UI is unverified (no settings page found).

name: Build with Google skill and MCP bundles
what: Onboarding and Settings offer curated bundles (web guidance, Firebase, Android, Flutter, Maps, Cloud, Chrome DevTools, science, data agent kit) that install skills and MCP servers for a stack.
how: GetBuildWithGooglePlugins / DownloadBuildWithGooglePlugin RPCs; onboarding step that installs selected bundles; Settings > Customizations > Build with Google Plugins; bundles are mostly SKILL.md folders plus optional MCP servers.
verevonRelevance: A vendor-curated starter-pack concept for Verevon: org-level skill/connector bundles installed at onboarding (ties to the skills registry, baseline s5).
notes: Bundle list from DOC; install RPCs from the binary.

name: Workspace API tool for first-party service calls
what: A generic tool lets the agent call an authenticated HTTP API of the host workspace with a description of why, optionally restricted to read-only.
how: CortexStepWorkspaceAPI {url, http_method, body, description, status_code, response}; WorkspaceAPIToolConfig.read_only; settings WorkspaceApiConfig in unified state.
verevonRelevance: Equivalent to Verevon execute_provider_action; the read_only switch at tool-config level is a simple safety pattern.
notes: Purpose inferred from field names; no UI copy found.

name: Typed step trajectory ("Cascade") as the agent data model
what: Every agent turn is a numbered sequence of typed steps (model response, tool call, user input, checkpoint, system message...) with status, source and timing, so any step can be rendered, queued, cancelled, forked or reverted.
how: gemini_coder.Trajectory holds Step records; CortexStepType has 118 values including UNSPECIFIED (planner response, run command, view file, browser steps, task boundary, notify user, invoke subagent, checkpoint, ephemeral message...); CortexStepStatus GENERATING, QUEUED, PENDING, RUNNING, WAITING, DONE, INVALID, CLEARED, CANCELED, ERROR, INTERRUPTED; CortexStepSource MODEL, USER_IMPLICIT, USER_EXPLICIT, SYSTEM, SYSTEM_SDK; CortexStepMetadata stores created/viewable/started/completed times, tool call (original and modified), model usage, retry infos, credits, hook results and snapshot metadata; CascadeRunStatus IDLE, RUNNING, CANCELING, BUSY.
verevonRelevance: session-core already owns threads, runs and events as append-only rows (baseline s4/s13); a uniform typed step record with status transitions per step is what makes revert, fork, queue and per-step cost possible.
notes: Quality 5: the single most reusable idea in the app. 467 messages in cortex.proto alone; surface is large and partly Google-internal.

name: Executor loop controls and termination reasons
what: The loop has explicit knobs for maximum model invocations, forced continuations, terminal step types, a required finish tool, checkpoint holds and stop-hook continuations, and records why it stopped.
how: CascadeExecutorConfig {disable_async, max_generator_invocations, terminal_step_types, hold_for_valid_checkpoint(+timeout), research_only, use_aggressive_snapshotting, require_finish_tool, max_forced_invocations, queue_all_steps, enable_tasks, enable_afk_stop_hook, max_stop_hook_continuations, enable_hook_status}; ExecutorTerminationReason ERROR, USER_CANCELED, MAX_INVOCATIONS, NO_TOOL_CALL, MAX_FORCED_INVOCATIONS, EARLY_CONTINUE, TERMINAL_STEP_TYPE, TERMINAL_CUSTOM_HOOK, INJECTED_RESPONSE, MAX_TOKEN_BUDGET_EXCEEDED; ExecutorMetadata records termination reason, invocation counts and snapshots before/after.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane has round and wall-clock budgets and "finalization_pending" receipts (baseline s4); a typed termination-reason enum and research_only mode would unify its logging and UI messages.

name: Task boundary tool and PLANNING/EXECUTION/VERIFICATION modes
what: The agent groups work into named tasks with a status and summary, declares which mode it is in (planning, execution, verification) and posts progress updates; the UI renders task groups with an overview, edited files and collapsible subtasks.
how: CortexStepTaskBoundary {task_name, task_status, task_summary (+with_citations), delta_summary (+with_citations), AgentMode PLANNING|EXECUTION|VERIFICATION}; TaskBoundaryToolConfig {minimum_predicted_task_size, target_status_update_frequency, soft and strict reminder thresholds when no task is active}; docs describe task groups, pending approval steps collected at the end of a group, and collapsed-by-default details.
verevonRelevance: Verevon shows plans/todos from orchestration and a Work panel (baseline s4, s10); a model-emitted task boundary with reminder thresholds gives a cheap, model-authored progress narrative that does not depend on server-side plan rows.
notes: Reminder thresholds nudge the model when it works without declaring a task; pattern worth copying for long runs.

name: Planning-mode prompt: plan only when warranted, then gate
what: In planning mode the agent researches without modifying sources, writes an implementation plan artifact with open questions, stops for explicit approval, executes, verifies, and writes a walkthrough; it skips planning for investigative or trivial requests.
how: Go-template system prompt sections embedded in the binary: Planning Mode (when to plan list, Research, Create Implementation Plan, Obtain User Approval, Execute, Verify; conditional on .IsAutonomous which removes the approval stop and request_feedback flags) and the planning-artifacts template defining implementation_plan.md (goal, user review required with alert callouts, open questions, proposed changes grouped by component with [NEW]/[MODIFY]/[DELETE] file markers, verification plan) and walkthrough.md. Plan artifacts set ArtifactMetadata.request_feedback and user_facing.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plan_proposed is a structured step list with an authority rung (baseline s4); adopt the "plan only when warranted" rubric and the plan-document format with a user-review-required section and verification plan.
notes: Prompt wording paraphrased. This build says planning mode is no longer supported in the UI copy and exposes /plan instead; the template still ships (agentic_mode_config.use_slash_plan). Plan modes exist in peers; the distinct part is the when-to-plan rubric and the artifact format.

name: notify_user: blocking review request with confidence and auto-proceed
what: When the agent needs review it calls a notify tool naming the artifact paths to review, whether the call blocks, a confidence score with justification, and whether it may auto-proceed; the artifact review policy decides if the user must approve.
how: CortexStepNotifyUser {review_absolute_uris, notification_content, is_blocking, confidence_score, confidence_justification, should_auto_proceed, diffs_uri, ask_for_user_feedback}; NotifyUserConfig.artifact_review_mode (ArtifactReviewMode ALWAYS, TURBO, AUTO); settings Request review vs Always proceed (docs); OS notification when the agent finishes or needs attention.
verevonRelevance: Verevon approvals are per tool or per plan; a model-reported confidence_score tied to an AUTO review mode (proceed when confident, ask when not) is a new gating signal Model Plane could pair with its deterministic confidence score.
notes: Model-self-reported confidence is weakly calibrated; treat it as a hint beside checks, as Verevon already does with verification passes.

name: Review comments feed the next agent turn
what: Comments left on artifacts (selected text), on file diffs and on files are attached to the next user message so the agent revises before changing anything; approving the plan is a separate Proceed action.
how: CortexStepUserInput carries repeated ArtifactComment (full file or selections, approval_status APPROVED|REQUESTED_CHANGES), FileDiffComment {file_uri, DiffCommentInfo with original/modified selections}, and FileComment; SendUserCascadeMessageRequest has the same fields; ArtifactReviewState PENDING_REVIEW, REVIEWED, MODIFIED with last_reviewed_content; UI batch comment events and Proceed with Plan button.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plan card has edit/approve/reject (baseline s4) but no text-anchored comments; structured comments as an input type on the next run request is the missing contract between UI and execution-core.
notes: Quality 5: the central human-in-the-loop idea of the product, built into the data model rather than chat text.

name: Autonomous mode
what: A toolbar toggle puts the agent in a mode where it works independently, asks no questions and requests no new permissions; the plan-approval stop disappears.
how: CascadePlannerConfig.autonomous; prompt templates branch on IsAutonomous; UI row autonomous-mode-switch with explanatory tooltip and the jetski.autonomousMode flag; docs: Always proceed review policy is described as a fully autonomous workflow.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane autonomy rungs (read_only, workspace_write, danger_full_access) already exist; an explicit "autonomous" flag that also suppresses ask_question and plan stops is the behavioural half that is missing.

name: Subagents: spec, workspace modes, model tiers and nesting cap
what: The main agent can start subagents with their own context, role, prompt, workspace (inherit, a branch/worktree, another folder or a shared directory), model tier, and either as normal runs or as background tasks; nesting depth is capped.
how: SubagentSpec {type_name, role, initial_prompt, workspace inherit|branch|workspace_uri|share, model, ModelTier INHERIT|FLASH_LITE|FLASH|PRO, run_as_task, fork}; InvokeSubagentToolConfig {fast_model, heavy_model, max_nesting_depth, allow_task_mode, always_inherit_model, allow_fork}; CortexStepInvokeSubagent returns SubagentResult {conversation_id, log uri, workspace uris}; tools invoke_subagent, manage_subagents (kill), define_subagent (system prompt, MCP/write/subagent grants), send_message; docs: nesting up to 10, built-in research/browser/self agents, subagent inherits permission scopes but not conversation history.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane subagents are depth-1 with isolated history and a ceiling of 100 children (baseline s4); model-tier selection per subagent and optional run_as_task are direct cost/latency levers.

name: Agent mailbox: prioritised messages between agents
what: Agents and sidecars can message each other (and the user-visible parent) with priority and delivery timing; pending messages are streamed to the UI and can be deleted.
how: AgentMessage {id, recipient, sender, priority LOW|NORMAL|HIGH, timestamp, render_details, hide_from_user, content or step_payload, source_metadata, delivery_strategy NEXT_INVOCATION|WHEN_IDLE}; SendAgentMessage/DeleteAgentMessage RPCs; PendingAgentMessagesUpdate in the state stream; GetAgentTeamMetadata lists AgentInstance and AgentTeamTask.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no agent-to-agent channel (A2A not built, baseline s5); a persisted mailbox with delivery strategy is a simple substrate for subagent results and run watchers.

name: Background tasks and commands as first-class state
what: Long commands and MCP tools can move to the background; the UI lists them with logs and lets the user cancel, and the loop reports when everything is idle.
how: manage_task tool (list, kill, status, send_input); TaskSnapshot {task_id, tool_name, summary, start_time, step_index, log_uri, is_daemon}; BackgroundCommand; SendStepsToBackground RPC; McpToolBackgroundMode OFF|ALWAYS with McpTaskOptions; run_persistent and daemon commands on RunCommand; fully_idle flag on every update; checkpoints record running tasks.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has Space-scoped process tools and "notify me when done" watchers (baseline s4); exposing background tasks as a typed list on the run (with fully_idle) fits the existing process_* tools.

name: Checkpoint compaction with a structured summary
what: When context grows, the system writes a checkpoint step containing the conversation title, user intent, session summary, code-change summary, artifact snapshots, running-task and subagent snapshots, so the model can continue with a small prompt.
how: CheckpointConfig {token_threshold, max_overhead_ratio, moving_window_size, max_token_limit, checkpoint_model, full_async, strategy SAME_MODEL|SINGLE_PROMPT, enable_fallback, include_artifact/subagent/running_task snapshots, include_conversation_log, prompt overrides}; CortexStepCheckpoint {user_intent, session_summary, code_change_summary, edited_file_map, memory_summary, accumulated_sections, user_requests}; CompactionInfo lists compacted step indices; UI flags Model Summarization Failed / Fallback Summary Used.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane compacts in two tiers and offers reattach_context (baseline s4); the structured checkpoint schema and explicit fallback summary give compaction a typed, inspectable shape.

name: Context-window accounting and truncation reasons
what: Each model call records estimated tokens used, the maximum, whether truncation happened and why (cache TTL expiry or token limit), and a breakdown by system prompt, tools, rules, MCP tools, skills, subagents, messages, workflows and plugins.
how: ContextWindowMetadata {estimated_tokens_used, truncation_reason PROMPT_CACHE_TTL_EXPIRED|MAX_TOKEN_LIMIT, token_breakdown, max_context_tokens}; TokenBreakdown groups with TokenType and TokenSource; server message that a prefix was cleared when the conversation grew too large; custom-model dialog exposes a compaction threshold.
verevonRelevance: Verevon context inspector shows tokens per segment (baseline s10); adding truncation_reason and a cache-TTL cause would explain unexpected forgetting.

name: Ephemeral messages with persistence levels
what: The harness injects short-lived reminders and observations (heuristic prompts, browser screenshot or DOM) into the next model call and can keep all of them or only the latest.
how: EphemeralMessagesConfig {persistence_level ALL|LATEST_ONLY, browser_ephemeral_options SCREENSHOT|DOM, enabled/disabled heuristics, heuristic_prompts, static_messages}; CortexStepEphemeralMessage {content, media, triggered_heuristics, dom_tree_uri}; hooks can inject ephemeral messages too.
verevonRelevance: A clean way to feed transient browser observations or policy reminders to Model Plane loops without polluting stored history or ZDR-sensitive transcripts.
notes: LATEST_ONLY keeps token cost flat for screenshot loops.

name: Lifecycle hooks with a JSON contract and step injection
what: Users attach scripts to six events (session start, pre/post tool use, pre/post model call, stop); a pre-tool hook can allow, auto-approve, deny, ask, force-ask or deny-unless-granted, rewrite arguments, and override permissions; other hooks can inject steps or force the loop to continue or end.
how: hooks.json (workspace .agents/hooks.json or global config) with matcher regex on tool name; handler type command (shell, JSON on stdin/stdout, camelCase) or prompt (a model-evaluated PromptHook with its own model field); HookArgsCommon passes conversation id, workspace paths, transcript path, artifact directory, execution id, model name, is_battle_mode, last user input; PreToolHookResult {decision, reason, overwrite, permission_overrides}; PostInvocationHookResult {inject_steps, termination_behavior}; StopHookResult decision continue; injected steps may be tool calls, system, user or ephemeral messages; HookStatus shown in the UI.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane hooks are real but not applied in Do mode and live in gateway memory (baseline known gap 4); this contract (six events, decisions, injected steps, prompt hooks) is a ready spec for wiring them into execution-core.
notes: PostToolUse cannot change the outcome per docs. Hook UI supports add/edit handlers and shows saving to hooks.json. All sibling inventories list hooks; Antigravity has fewer events than Claude Code but adds prompt hooks and step injection.

name: Retry and self-correction policy
what: Model-output errors (bad tool JSON) and API errors have separate retry policies; the retry can forbid tools or force a specific tool on the last attempt; loops are detected and the looping reply is dropped.
how: PlannerRetryConfig {ModelOutputRetryConfig(max_retries, forbid_tool_use|force_tool_name, retry_only_on_invalid_args), ModelAPIRetryConfig(initial sleep, exponential multiplier, error feedback, jitter range)}; RetryReason API_RETRYABLE, MODEL_CORRECTABLE, NON_RECOVERABLE; TrajectoryConversionConfig discard_looping_planner_responses, discard_errored_planner_responses; stop reasons CLIENT_LOOPING, TOOL_PARSE_ERROR, INVALID_MESSAGE_ORDER; a correction prompt tells the model to retry tool calls one at a time.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane already retries transient tool failures (baseline s4); separating model-correctable from API-retryable errors and loop detection are the missing categories.

name: Parallel tool calls and async execution levels
what: The agent is instructed to batch independent calls and the executor can run tools fully asynchronously or block per invocation; the UI shows queue wait vs execution time.
how: Batch function-calling prompt section; ExecutionAsyncLevel INVOCATION_BLOCKING|EXECUTOR_BLOCKING|FULL_ASYNC; CortexStepMetadata.wait_for_previous_tools and CascadePlannerConfig.no_wait_for_previous_tools; trajectory debug timeline splits queue wait from tool execution.
verevonRelevance: Both Verevon loops already use join_all (baseline s4); an explicit ordering flag per tool plus a visible queue-wait metric would help diagnose slow runs.

name: Scheduled tasks and automations spawn agents on a cron
what: Users create scheduled tasks (cron or minute-level schedules with a prompt and a project) and install automations that run as background processes and start conversations; each run is visible with logs and events.
how: ScheduleToolConfig; sidecar manifest builtin "schedule" with five-field cron; agentapi new-conversation and send-message commands available to sidecars; UI scheduled tasks page (task name, cron expression, prompt, project, events, logs, delete) and an Automations list with argument forms; SidecarEvent records send_message/new_conversation payloads; automation agents get explicit permissions (SidecarAgentPermissions: workspace_uris, access_grants, allows_user_interactions) while the automation code itself is trusted.
verevonRelevance: Verevon scheduled runs are one no-tool 1,024-token call with no delivery (baseline known gap 6); scheduling a full agent run with explicit grants and a visible event log is the upgrade.
notes: Windows desktop builds: schedule runs only while the hub app or daemon is alive.

name: /goal continuation loop and goal state
what: The user states an objective and the agent keeps working, building, diagnosing and fixing without stopping for confirmation until the goal completes or is cancelled.
how: GoalState {goal_text, started_at, start_step_index, continuation_count, State ACTIVE|COMPLETED|CANCELLED}; enable_afk_stop_hook and max_stop_hook_continuations in the executor; stop hooks can decide continue; docs list /goal among slash commands.
verevonRelevance: Equivalent to a durable goal on a Verevon run with a continuation counter; maps to Temporal DeepTask which chat and Do do not use today (baseline s4).
notes: Behaviour from DOC plus the state message; stop-hook linkage is inferred.

name: /boost multi-agent reasoning pipeline
what: An on-demand mode for hard bugs where an orchestrator splits work into implementation, investigation and verification subagents that run in clean scopes, test hypotheses by building and running tests, and synthesise verified changes.
how: Docs describe three phases (strategy, parallel execution and verification, synthesis) with read-only investigation subagents and verification subagents that run build targets; the binary ships built-in role agents and orchestrator descriptions; paid plan only.
verevonRelevance: A named reasoning workflow users can invoke; Model Plane has an EvaluatorOptimizer workflow reachable only via StartWorkflow (baseline s4) that could be exposed behind a slash command.
notes: Mechanism details come from the public docs page; roles are in the binary but not decoded.

name: Teamwork preview: long-running multi-agent projects with gates
what: For multi-day work a scoping interview produces a prompt artifact, then a Sentinel coordinates a Project Orchestrator, explorers, workers and verification gates (critic, challenger, auditor, success auditor) with request, plan and progress artifacts and integrity modes.
how: Docs: spec-plan interview, milestones, fresh successor orchestrator per milestone to avoid context rot, one worker per file, Alt+J jumps to waiting subagents, integrity modes development/demo/benchmark. Binary: enable_teamwork_subagent customization flag and about 30 teamwork_preview_* role identifiers (layer, referee, explorer, proof, curator, worker, solver, falsifier, patcher, reviewer, outliner, judge, implementer, mergers, replanner, victory auditor...), swarm/blackboard/conductor conventions in embedded prompts, GetAgentTeamMetadata RPC.
verevonRelevance: Shows a production pattern for long horizons (state in artifacts, successor orchestrator per milestone, independent verifier roles); relevant to Verevon DeepTask/WideResearch workflows but only as a design reference.
notes: Marked preview and paid-plan only; role semantics beyond names come from DOC. Peer inventories mention teams or swarms (deepseek, hermes); compare in the cross-source synthesis.

name: Best of N: parallel attempts in isolated clones with a winner
what: One prompt can be run as N parallel attempts (different models or the same model) in separate workspace clones; the user compares and picks a winner whose changes are applied back; the system can auto-trigger it and record preference reasons.
how: StartBattleModeRequest {requests, num_forks, models, fork_at_step_index, auto_triggered, agent_scripts, clone_strategy}; BattleModeInfo {children, winning_conversation_id, models, eliminated, end_type WINNER|TIE|KILL|SKIP|REFERENCE|START_ERROR, clone_strategy}; CloneStrategy git OVERLAY vs full CLONE (setting to use full git clones so commits survive); EndBattleMode/EliminateBattleModeArm; DetectBattleModeAutoTrigger returns target N, tag and banner text; UI offers Enable Best-of-2 prompts, opt-out reasons, a pick-at-most-2 reasons chooser and Revert and redo turn using N trajectories.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no model comparison (baseline s9 absent); an arms-per-prompt mode over sandbox-manager leases with winner selection is feasible and doubles as a preference-data collector.
notes: Custom agents are disabled in Best-of-N; cannot start while subagents or background tasks run. No sibling inventory lists best-of-N; Cursor (not inventoried here) is known to offer parallel multi-model attempts, so treated as uncommon rather than unique.

name: Error classes surfaced as actionable agent states
what: Terminal agent errors, quota exhaustion, insufficient credits, verification required, offline and language-server loss each produce a specific banner with the right next action (try again, select another model, buy credits, verify account).
how: CortexErrorDetails {user_error_message, model_error_message, structured_error_parts (text, file, directory, url, code), short/full error, is_benign, error_id, rpc details}; UI strings for model quota reached, baseline model quota reached, insufficient AI credits with purchase button, verification required, lost connection to the language server and no internet.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has typed failure actions (baseline s1 "Failure presentation"); structured_error_parts that carry file/url references are an additional rendering contract.

name: Skills with progressive disclosure and slash invocation
what: A skill is a folder with SKILL.md (name, description, instructions, optional scripts/examples/resources); the agent sees only names and descriptions until it decides to open one, and the user can invoke any skill as /name.
how: Discovery paths per surface (workspace .agents/skills, global config skills); GetAllSkills, ScanSkillsConfigFile, DeleteSkill, skill_search tool (SkillSearchToolConfig), SkillsConfig {preload_skill_names, builtin_skill_names, inherit_user}; SlashCommandType SKILL; skills count toward a customization token budget; Agent Market search for community skills.
verevonRelevance: Verevon skills have trigger keywords, file patterns and a skills budget with reattach_skill (baseline s5); the SKILL.md open-standard layout and a marketplace search would make skills portable.
notes: Docs say workflows are being deprecated in favour of skills; UI offers an agent-run migration.

name: Rules with four activation modes and a token budget
what: Rules are Markdown instructions discovered up the directory tree (AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, .agents/rules/*.md) with activation modes always_on, model_decision, glob and manual; oversized rules are demoted to pointers.
how: Rules frontmatter trigger values map to CortexMemoryTrigger ALWAYS_ON, MODEL_DECISION, MANUAL, GLOB; CortexMemoryProjectScope {globs, description, priority}; DIRECTORY_RULES step injects rules when a file in that directory is touched; docs: 24,000-byte per-file cap, 20,000-token budget for global and always-on rules, @[label](path) includes; UI context-usage meter shows percent of the customization budget.
verevonRelevance: Verevon layers org, Space and persona instructions only in Ask turns and not in Do runs (baseline known gap 2); the four trigger modes and a demotion budget are the model to bring instructions into Do mode safely.
notes: Four activation modes mirror Cursor-style rule types.

name: Plugin bundles with marketplace and per-plugin context cost
what: A plugin is a directory (plugin.json) bundling skills, agents, rules, MCP servers and hooks; users browse a marketplace, install, enable or disable, and each plugin page lists the commands, skills, agents, MCP servers and token cost it adds.
how: cascade_plugins proto (CascadePluginTemplate with commands, local and remote config, installation_count, trust_level, readme; Get/Install RPCs); UserConfig.plugins with MarketplaceInstall provenance; GetAllPlugins/GetPlugin/DeletePlugin; plugin details view shows slash commands, delegated agents, MCP servers, hooks, UI extensions and a context-usage bar; Create with Prompt lets the agent scaffold a plugin; official marketplace id antigravity-plugins-official.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plugins registry is inert with no marketplace or install flow (baseline s5, known gap 11); manifest + provenance + token-cost display is a working template.
notes: trust_level on templates suggests curated vs community tiers; semantics unverified.

name: Sidecars: managed background processes with UI panes
what: Sidecars are local processes declared in sidecar.json (command or builtin scheduler, args, env, restart policy) that Antigravity launches, restarts, and can expose as full-pane or auxiliary-pane web UIs; they call back through an agentapi CLI.
how: SidecarConfig {command|builtin, restart_policy, args, env, display_name, has_web_ui, ui_config with SidecarUIView entrypoints AUX_PANE|FULL_PANE, agent_permissions, arguments}; SidecarStatus RUNNING|STOPPED|ERRORED|BACKOFF; ManageSidecar RPC actions; sidecar UI served through the privileged plugin:// scheme into an iframe with a UI token; per-sidecar data/logs/events directories; sidecars disabled by default and enabled per id in config.json.
verevonRelevance: A cheap extension seam for Verevon: declarative background workers with UI panes and a narrow agent API, instead of embedding every integration in Rust or Go services.
notes: Docs do not describe a sandbox for sidecar code; the proto only limits the agents they spawn. The manus inventory also uses the word sidecar; semantics differ, check in synthesis.

name: Declarative agent assembly: custom agents, prompt sections and profiles
what: Agents can be defined as Markdown, JSON, command or Python scripts, picking model tier, tool lists, MCP servers, hooks and system-prompt sections; prompt sections can be removed, added, appended or replaced by name; profiles inherit from each other with per-type exclusions.
how: CustomAgentSpec / AgentConfig / DeclarativeComponentConfig {function providers (MCP), prompt sections, named tools, hooks by phase, tool decorators, resolution policy}; PromptSectionCustomizationConfig (remove/add/append/replace); AgentScriptItem {command_spec|python_spec|config_path|config|cascade_config, subagent, main_agent, model_tier}; ProfileConfig {inherit, per-type CustomizationSourceConfig for skills/agents/plugins/hooks/mcp/rules}; UI Customization Profile [Beta].
verevonRelevance: Gives a concrete schema for Verevon "Space agents" and blueprints that today are labelled not-yet-configured (baseline s4 Agents overview).

name: MCP client with OAuth, per-tool controls and background mode
what: MCP servers (stdio or Streamable HTTP/SSE) are managed in a store-like UI with OAuth and Google-credential auth, per-server and per-tool enable switches, lazy loading, elicitation prompts and a state panel showing status, tools and errors.
how: McpServerSpec {command/args/env/cwd or server_url/headers, disabled_tools, enabled_tools, oauth client id/secret, auth_provider_type GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS, timeout, strict_argument_validation, omit_from_system_prompt, force_all_tools_eager, disable_standalone_sse}; McpServerState {status PENDING|READY|ERROR|DISABLED_BY_ADMIN, tools, tool_errors, instructions, auth_url}; McpToolConfig.enable_lazy_load; ElicitationInteraction; ListMcpResources/ListMcpPrompts/GetMcpPrompt; mcp(server/tool) permission patterns; CompleteMcpOAuth/DisconnectMcpOAuth.
verevonRelevance: Verevon registers MCP servers with OAuth but both loops deny mcp__ tools (baseline known gap 1); enabled/disabled tool lists, lazy loading and an admin-disable state are details to finish when execution is wired.

name: Slash commands as an agent-facing command bus
what: Built-in commands cover planning, goals, boost, teamwork, learning, scheduling, browser control, side questions, plugins, resuming, rewinding, permissions, model choice, usage and voice; skills are surfaced as commands too.
how: Docs list /plan, /grill-me, /goal, /boost, /teamwork-preview, /learn, /plugin, /schedule, /browser, /btw plus CLI /resume, /rewind, /rename, /permissions, /model, /keybindings, /statusline, /tasks, /skills, /mcp, /diff, /remote-control, /usage; GetSlashCommands returns SlashCommandDefinition with arguments; /grill-me interviews the user before coding; /learn distils corrections into rules or skills.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has five built-in slash commands and no user-authored templates (baseline s5); /plan, /goal, /grill-me and /learn are the highest-value additions.

name: Python SDK and headless CLI over the same harness
what: The same agent harness is exposed as a Python SDK (Agent, LocalAgentConfig, policies, hooks, triggers, subagents, structured output, session save/restore) and as an agy CLI with headless mode for CI.
how: Docs: pip package google-antigravity; async Agent context manager; policy helpers allow/deny/ask_user; local models via LiteRT or OpenAI-compatible servers; response_schema (Pydantic); conversation_id restore; the binary lists CORTEX_TRAJECTORY_SOURCE_SDK and CLI and the SDK_EXECUTABLE message origin.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has generated SDK tests and an AG-UI adapter with no consumer (baseline s5); a thin SDK over Model Plane runs with policy callbacks would give customers the same harness the app uses.

name: Import from Cursor and AI Studio
what: The app can import Cursor settings/rules and AI Studio projects (offering the Firebase skill when relevant) to lower switching cost.
how: ImportFromCursor RPC {source_path} returning copied, duplicate and problem files; UI events for importing rules from Cursor; ImportProjectFromUrl and an Import AI Studio Project flow; onboarding has an import page and a migration-scope page.
verevonRelevance: An import-from-competitor path (Claude/ChatGPT exports, Cursor rules) is an adoption lever Verevon lacks (baseline s1 import absent).

name: Fine-grained GitHub permission policies for the agent
what: Users can authorise the agent for GitHub with per-repository policies: read access, issue creation, pull-request creation, branch create/update/delete patterns, workflow run visibility and dispatch, with lists or wildcards of numbers and branch globs.
how: Settings page for GitHub permissions; GitHub personal access token validated against GitHub and stored with the username in the user home env file; policies per org and repository with access rules text such as comma lists or *; ProjectSettings.enable_permissioned_github.
verevonRelevance: A resource-scoped permission model per integration; Verevon provider actions already pass through capability policy, so per-repo/branch allowlists can reuse that engine.
notes: Token stored in a plaintext dotfile (string evidence); weak secret handling, avoid.

name: Browser subagent with its own model and recording
what: A dedicated browser agent runs a delegated web task with its own model, context policy and tool budget, returns a result, records the session, and can be skipped or reused by the main agent.
how: CortexStepBrowserSubagent {task, task_name, task_summary, result, subagent_id, reused_subagent_id, recording_path/name, RecordingGenerationStatus, scratchpad_path, skipped}; BrowserSubagentToolConfig {mode MAIN_AGENT_ONLY|SUBAGENT_PRIMARILY|BOTH|SUBAGENT_ONLY, browser_subagent_model, suggested_max_tool_calls, max_context_tokens, context_config WITH_MARKDOWN_TRAJECTORY_SUMMARY|TASK_ONLY, reminder modes (verify screenshots, verify completeness, custom), enable_scratchpad}; SkipBrowserSubagent RPC; slash command /browser.
verevonRelevance: Fits the rule that the Model proposes and Quarry executes: a browser-subagent run with its own model/budget and recording is the Model Plane side of Quarry sessions (agent browser runs currently fail closed, baseline gap 5).
notes: Quality 5: recording, scratchpad, reminders and context modes are all configurable per deployment.

name: Browser toolset modes and per-action state diffs
what: The browser agent can use full DOM-index tools, pixel-only tools, or DOM input with pixel output; after every action the harness returns a compact diff of browser state instead of a new full snapshot.
how: BrowserToolSetMode ALL_TOOLS|PIXEL_ONLY|ALL_INPUT_PIXEL_OUTPUT; BrowserStateDiffingConfig {capture_agent_action_diffs, include_dom_tree_in_diffs}; each browser step carries browser_state_diff; get_dom returns only interactive elements and text in the viewport with indices; click-by-pixel, drag path, mouse wheel, move, down/up steps; ClickFeedbackConfig draws a dot or mouse pointer overlay in screenshots.
verevonRelevance: Quarry returns observations after proposed actions; sending a state diff (and an optional pixel-only mode for Computer-Use style models) cuts tokens and aligns with future Gemini computer-use routes.

name: Two-layer browser access control and action permissions
what: Pages must pass a server-side denylist (hostname check that fails closed) and the user allowlist (starts with localhost, grown via an Always allow prompt); reading a page and acting on it are separate permissions, and page JavaScript has its own policy.
how: BrowserAllowlistConfig, AddToBrowserWhitelist/GetAllBrowserWhitelistedUrls RPCs; BrowserActionWaitingReason PAGE_ACCESS|ACTION_PERMISSION|both; permission resources read_url vs execute_url; BrowserJsExecutionPolicy DISABLED|ALWAYS_ASK|MODEL_DECIDES|TURBO; UI lists denied sites and not-yet-allowlisted sites per run and offers Add to allowlist; admin blocks show Feature Disabled.
verevonRelevance: Maps onto Quarry risk classes (login, checkout, cross-domain); a separate read-vs-act permission and a model-decides JS policy refine the grant that the broker never mints today (baseline gap 5).
notes: Denylist depends on a Google service; the allowlist is a local file.

name: Browser session recording as a reviewable artifact
what: Browser tasks produce a video recording that plays below the step and is stored as an artifact looping through the agent actions; the walkthrough can embed screenshots and recordings.
how: webm_encoder.exe consumes DevTools screencast frames and writes WebM (VP9); RecordingGenerationStatus GENERATING|ERROR|COMPLETED; generate_recording_synchronously option; UI shows rendering playback and playback available states and an Error loading Browser recording state.
verevonRelevance: Strong evidence UX for Verevon proof bundles: attach a recording or frame strip to the run receipt for browser procedures.
notes: Recording is generated client-side by a helper binary; not guaranteed ("when available").

name: Embedded Chrome DevTools MCP and WebMCP
what: The app bundles a Chrome DevTools MCP server so the agent can navigate, click, fill, inspect network and console, take heap snapshots, run Lighthouse and performance traces, drive Chrome extensions and call tools that web pages expose.
how: chrome-devtools-mcp 1.1.0 unpacked under app.asar.unpacked; tool groups for navigation, input, inspection, emulation, performance, memory, screencast, extensions and webmcp (list/execute); launched against a separate Chrome profile on a configurable CDP port with a Chrome path override; telemetry and update checks have env opt-outs (whether Antigravity sets them is unverified).
verevonRelevance: Confirms a pattern: ship an MCP browser server for the agent rather than invent tools; Quarry already owns this, so the useful part is WebMCP discovery and the lighthouse/performance tools.
notes: REA module list from the scout (REA-JS) plus package.json; not re-run here.

name: Terminal command execution with sandbox and bypass modes
what: Commands run in a persistent PTY shell; by default inside an OS sandbox (workspace read/write, no network); the model must request bypass for network or outside access and the user approves with scope choices.
how: RunCommandToolConfig {enable_pty, enable_persistent_mode, enable_terminal_sandbox, shell_setup_script, max_timeout_ms, execution_host, enable_daemon_commands, search_fallback_mode}; CortexStepRunCommand {sandbox_override, ran_in_sandbox, sandbox_errors, auto_run_decision, is_daemon, combined_output with truncation}; CommandStatusToolConfig {delta output, stabilization wait, input detection model}; CascadeRunCommandInteraction {confirm, submitted command line, sandbox_override}; embedded prompt explains Standard vs Bypass sandbox and says try sandboxed first.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane has bwrap/Landlock for Linux only and a shell tool that is not in the Do catalogue (baseline s6); the standard-vs-bypass distinction with explicit user approval is the UX to copy once shell is offered.
notes: command_status can use a small model to detect that a command is waiting for input.

name: OS-level terminal sandbox with network allowlist
what: Terminal commands can be confined by OS isolation without VMs: Linux namespaces, macOS Seatbelt, a Windows AppContainer helper; network is off unless the allowed read_url domains are added; sensitive paths such as ssh keys and env files are hidden.
how: Docs describe per-OS mechanisms, writable/readable/blocked sets and the allowlist coupling; LS carries a Windows sandbox helper (AppContainer profile create/delete); settings Enable Terminal Sandbox, Sandbox Allow Network, Commands Outside Sandbox lists; Windows exposes the sandbox as a Preview toggle that is not tied to the permission presets.
verevonRelevance: Validates Model Plane bwrap+Landlock+seccomp and suggests adding the network-allowlist-follows-read_url coupling and macOS/Windows backends only when a second sandbox backend is justified (ledger defers it).
notes: Mechanism per OS is from docs; Windows internals unverified.

name: Projects, environments and git worktrees for parallel agents
what: Projects bundle one or more folders (plain or git) with their own settings and permission grants; each conversation runs Local or in a new git worktree (also background workers) so parallel agents do not collide.
how: project.proto Project {resources, environments, permission_grants, settings, archived}; Resource folder|git_folder{default_branch, allow_write}; AgentEnvironment LOCAL|BACKGROUND_WORKTREE|...; CreateWorktree/CheckoutWorktree/DeleteWorktree/GetWorktreeDiff RPCs; GitCloneStrategy OVERLAY|CLONE; UI selectors for environment and branch, previous worktrees list, worktree available only for git repositories.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane rejected worktree isolation for subagents in its ledger and is not a coding product (baseline s6); the Project + Environment object is still a clean model for Verevon Spaces (resources, settings, grants per Space).

name: Remote Control: drive desktop agents from a browser
what: The desktop app registers with a cloud broker so the same UI can be opened in any browser or phone (QR code or link) to view conversations, review plans and approve tool calls on the host machine; settings stay editable only on the host.
how: ApiService.ConnectInstanceV2 (client-initiated bidirectional stream) carries ProxyRequestV2/ProxyResponseV2 {request_id, rpc_path, headers, payload}; ListInstances/UpdateInstance/EvictInstance with InstanceStatus CONNECTED|DISCONNECTED|IDLE; ProxyCommand/StreamProxyCommand route RPCs to a target instance uuid; mesh sessions use signalling messages with STUN/TURN servers and web-crypto public keys (RemoteControlDetails.Transport WEB_CHANNEL or WEB_RTC_DATA_CHANNEL); RegisterWebPush for notifications; telemetry events for session start/end and reconnect attempts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon runs in the cloud so it needs no tunnel, but this shows how to let a customer-hosted Model Plane or Support Plane runner be driven from the web UI via an outbound-only reverse RPC proxy.
notes: Docs: host must stay online and awake; access tied to the Google account; no encryption details documented. The claude and codex inventories also list remote-control features.

name: Remote and multi-hop workspaces
what: Users can add remote workspaces over SSH (setup window flow) and the language server can connect to saved or auto-detected remotes through multi-hop descriptors with interactive prompts.
how: RemotingService ConnectRemote (streamed prompts or status), RespondToPrompt (secret flag), Save/Delete/ListRemotes, ListConnectedRemotes; RemoteDescriptor {remote_multi_hop, name, description, type}; UI Add recent remote workspace and Open SSH connection in setup window.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Support Plane / remote-core style sessions; the multi-hop descriptor and prompt-response protocol could back customer-network agents.
notes: Transport and trust model unverified.

name: Web preview, deploy and cloud provisioning steps
what: The agent can start a dev server, show it in an embedded preview with an address bar (warning when sites block embedding), deploy a web app to a managed subdomain with a claim URL, and provision Firebase or Cloud SQL.
how: Steps RESTART_DEV_SERVER, DEPLOY_WEB_APP (subdomain, framework, file upload status, claim_url, deploy targets), CHECK_DEPLOY_STATUS, SET_UP_FIREBASE, DEPLOY_FIREBASE, SET_UP_CLOUD_SQL, CLOUD_SQL_EXECUTE_SQL and schema update; applet steps COMPILE_APPLET, LINT_APPLET, INSTALL_APPLET_PACKAGE; UI Web Preview pane with open-in-new-tab fallback.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is not a builder; the only portable idea is an embedded preview pane with an explicit framing-failure fallback for generated HTML artifacts.
notes: Deploy targets are Google-specific.

name: Git/VCS panel with LLM commit messages and push outcomes
what: A VCS panel shows agent edits, staged changes and branch changes per file with stage/unstage/discard, generates commit messages from the changes and conversation, pushes, and links to the new pull request or merge request.
how: GitStage/GitUnstage/GitCommit/GitDiscard/GitPush and GenerateCommitMessage RPCs; WatchVersionControlState; trajectory type COMMIT_MESSAGE_GENERATION; push result handling for GitHub, GitLab and Gerrit; TaskResolutionOpenPr {pr_title, pr_body, pr_url}.
verevonRelevance: Out of scope for a non-IDE product beyond the pattern of a task-resolution step (open PR) as a terminal action on a run.

name: Computer-use model hook but only browser-scoped control
what: The model enum includes an experimental computer-use Gemini model, yet the agent tools control only the browser (pixel and DOM) and terminal; there is no desktop-wide mouse and keyboard tool.
how: Model GOOGLE_GEMINI_COMPUTER_USE_EXPERIMENTAL in the Model enum; browser pixel steps (click pixel, drag pixel-to-pixel, mouse wheel); no desktop control step types among the 118 step-type values.

name: Local and OpenAI-compatible models through the SDK

verevonRelevance: Verevon has no explicit local model provider (baseline s9); the lightweight preset idea (fewer tools, shorter system prompt, tighter compaction) is the part worth copying for any small-context route.

name: Credits, quotas and overage controls

name: Per-turn and cumulative cost breakdown by token category

name: Four permission presets with per-project override
what: A single selector chooses Request Review (every command asks), Default (sandboxed commands auto-run, others ask), Vetted beta (a model-based guardian decides) or Turbo (everything allowed); each project can inherit the global preset or choose its own.
how: The UI maps each preset to a bundle of settings: terminal sandbox on/off, CascadeCommandsAutoExecution OFF|PROCEED_IN_SANDBOX|EAGER, non-workspace file policy ASK|ALLOW, and AgentPermissionPreset REQUEST_REVIEW|DEFAULT|VETTED|TURBO; ProjectSettings carries the same fields plus artifact_review_mode and shell_setup_script; new projects start with Inherit General; Vetted is offered only when a feature gate allows it.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane has autonomy rungs and capability policy (baseline s11); naming three or four presets that each set a bundle of enforceable settings, with per-Space override, makes the policy legible.
notes: Docs: macOS/Linux use the new preset system; Windows still shows older settings (Request Review, Proceed in Sandbox, Always Proceed). Comparable permission modes exist in Claude Code.

name: action(target) permission rules with deny > ask > allow and scopes
what: Every sensitive operation is a resource such as read_file(path), write_file(path), read_url(domain), execute_url(domain), command(prefix or regex), unsandboxed(...) or mcp(server/tool); rules in deny, ask and allow lists layer over the preset and deny always wins; an approval can be widened by scope.
how: PermissionResource {action, target}; PermissionGrantsConfig {allow, deny, ask}; PermissionScope ONCE|CONVERSATION|WORKSPACE|PROJECT|GLOBAL; PermissionInteraction {allow, scope, edited_target, persist_grants, user_deny_instruction, sandbox_override}; compound commands with command substitution or backticks disable prefix matching for the whole line; allowing a write implies the read, denying a read blocks the write; AllowAlwaysConfig lists dangerous binaries and subcommand tools that cannot be always-allowed.
verevonRelevance: A concrete grammar for Verevon capability grants (capability-core) with user-editable persistence and a safe widening ladder; the compound-command rule and dangerous-subcommand list are directly reusable for the shell tool.
notes: Per-project grants have a cross-project isolation trigger type, so a grant from one project cannot silently apply to another. The deny > ask > allow grammar resembles Claude Code permission rules; Antigravity adds a five-level scope ladder and compound-command handling.

name: Policy Guardian: a model-based security reviewer with vetting tools
what: In the Vetted preset a separate guardian model (itself a small agent with vetting tools) decides whether a proposed command should auto-run, checking data flow out of the machine, content, dependencies, shell environment changes, deletions and URLs, and repeated denied attempts.
how: PolicyGuardianConfig {enabled, model, fail_mode OPEN|CLOSED, antivirus_enabled/enforced, model_tier, vetted_tools, max_tool_rounds, enable_url_vetting, enable_denied_repeat_precheck, http_timeout_seconds}; CommandAssessorConfig {policy_guardian_config, active_tags}; the binary contains vet_data_flow, vet_content, vet_dependency, vet_shell_change, vet_deletion, vet_url and vet_denied_repeat identifiers and a per-command risk table (for example POST bodies to non-localhost URLs count as upload; untrusted package install counts as remote code execution).
verevonRelevance: A guardian-model pre-check between proposal and execution is the missing layer in execution-core (today a substring risk list, baseline known gap 14); keep it fail-closed and give it deterministic tools rather than free reasoning.
notes: Marked beta; fail_mode OPEN vs CLOSED is configurable, so correctness of the default is unverified. The codex inventory lists a guardian and the claude inventory an auto mode; similar in spirit.

name: Allow/deny command lists and system no-op list
