name: File access boundaries with reasons and prompts
what: The agent can read and write inside project folders and its data directory by default; reads outside the workspace or of gitignored files trigger a permission prompt stating why it was blocked, and "Agent Non-Workspace File Access" can be switched on.
how: FilePermissionInteractionSpec {path, is_directory, BlockReason OUTSIDE_WORKSPACE|GITIGNORED}; FileAccessPermission {path, allow, scope}; per-tool configs gate gitignore access; UI Allow in Conversation and Allow options; settings for non-workspace and gitignored file access.
verevonRelevance: Equivalent boundaries exist in Verevon as Space workspaces and sandbox leases; the typed block reason is a nice affordance for prompts.

name: Strict/secure mode and injection-risk warnings
what: A Strict Mode setting forces human review of every agent action and disables image rendering and browser JavaScript; the UI also warns that Always Proceed risks acting on unsafe or injected artifact content and lists autonomous execution, exfiltration, prompt injection and supply-chain risks.
how: UserSettings.secure_mode_enabled; UI copy for disabled-while-strict states; the shell wiring sets disableStrictMode in this build, and the docs page the UI links to returns 404; permission trigger type SECURE_MODE; warning text appears in the settings and onboarding agent page.
verevonRelevance: Corrects the earlier scout note that no prompt-injection phrase exists; for Verevon the useful part is stating the injection risk next to the autonomy control and tying a strict mode to a ZDR-like hard switch.
notes: The 2.0 build appears to disable strict mode while still shipping its copy; the docs link is dead, so the feature is half-retired.

name: Org policy locks and enterprise identity
what: Admins can lock settings, disable MCP or browser tools, pre-set allowed domains that users cannot remove, require licences by project and region, and use Google Cloud SSO or workforce identity federation; locked options display why.
how: FetchAdminControls and GetTeamOrganizationalControls RPCs; McpServerStatus DISABLED_BY_ADMIN; UI strings Disabled by organization policy, Blocked by organization policy, Feature Disabled (browser tools) and non-removable domain rules; sign-in options Continue with Google Cloud, advanced SSO, WIF config; licence selection by project and region; docs: data residency for third-party models limited to global, us or eu, and request/response logging to the customer project.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has SSO, org security and ZDR attestation controls (baseline s11); showing the reason a setting is locked and which layer locked it is a UX gap worth closing.

name: Permission review for installed automations
what: Installing an automation shows the arguments it needs and the permissions its spawned agents will receive; permissions can be reviewed and changed later from the automation menu, and automation code itself is treated as trusted.
how: SidecarUserConfig {enabled, project scope, argument_values, resolved_permissions}; SidecarAgentPermissions {workspace_uris, access_grants, allows_user_interactions}; UI two-step flow (Automation Arguments, Review Permissions) and Manage permissions.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for Verevon schedules and run watchers: show the capability grants a scheduled agent run will hold, with Control-signed decisions per Space effect.

name: Agent hub layout: sidebar, conversation, auxiliary pane and splits
what: A three-region layout: a sidebar of projects, workspaces and conversations; a central conversation; and an auxiliary pane that hosts artifacts, files, diffs, the browser subagent viewer, terminals, web preview and sidecar views; conversations can be split side by side.
how: Aux pane view types (File Viewer, Directory Viewer, Virtual File Viewer, Artifact Viewer, Global Artifact Viewer, Browser Subagent Viewer, Custom View, Sidecar View, Workspace File Explorer); split actions horizontal and vertical, remove from split, replace with new; persistent tabs cannot be closed; Toggle Auxiliary Pane; the hub app opens the IDE only as a separate app.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already moved to a calm conversation with a contextual canvas (Work, Output, Sources, Trace; baseline s12); multi-conversation splits and a file/diff/browser view registry in the canvas are the extension.

name: Command palette with typed pickers
what: Ctrl+P opens a command palette and Ctrl+Shift+P opens it with a command prefix; dedicated pickers search commands, files, conversations, projects and workspaces; code search has its own pane.
how: Shortcut table entries openCommandPalette, openCommandPaletteWithPrefix, openConvoPicker, openWorkspaceSelector, codeSearch; UI labels Command picker, File picker, Conversation picker, Project picker; context categories are provided to the composer through setContextCategories.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no command palette or shortcut sheet (baseline s12, planned I1); a typed picker registry (commands, threads, Spaces, agents, runs) is a high-leverage addition.

name: Keyboard-first design with 58 shortcuts and a shortcut overlay
what: Nearly every action has a shortcut with macOS overrides: accept/reject step (Alt+Enter, Alt+Shift+Backspace), new conversation, picker, model selector (Ctrl+/), voice (Ctrl+M), split, terminal, find, zoom and history actions (mark read/unread, archive, delete); a shortcut overlay lists them.
how: A declarative keybinding table with feature bindings and per-OS runtimeGating overrides (ctrl becomes mod on macOS); openShortcutsOverlay bound to Ctrl+?; actions disabled in some contexts; the table has 58 entries.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has Ctrl+Shift+O, Ctrl+I and thread switching (baseline s12); accepting or rejecting an agent step from the keyboard is the missing agentic shortcut.
notes: Full list in scratchpad/tmp/ag2/shortcuts.txt.

name: Attention model: notifications, sounds, tray and badges
what: The app tells the user when an agent needs input or finishes: OS notifications whose click opens the conversation, two distinct sounds (action required, done), a tray icon with the running-agent count, a sidebar attention state, web push for remote sessions and a quit confirmation when agents are active.
how: Redux middleware startOsConversationNotifications with sound files for cascadeDone and actionRequired; NotifyEvent in the cloud API; RegisterWebPush; settings Notification Preferences and Enable Notifications; shell tray with agent count and powerSaveBlocker option; Toggle Sidebar, conversations need attention.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has a "Notify me when done" watcher per run (baseline s4); distinguishing needs-input from finished, with different sound and sidebar state, is the UX that makes long runs usable.
notes: A favicon-badge feature is wired only for the internal app type. Windows defaults runInBackground off; keepComputerAwake is opt-in (scout).

name: Onboarding: wizard, import, setup pages and server-driven NUX tips
what: First run offers account options (Google, business account, Cloud project, SSO), theme, keyboard shortcut import, migration scope, Build with Google bundles and a post-onboarding sequence (manager welcome, usage mode, agent configuration, add workspace); contextual tips appear at server-defined places and triggers and are remembered once seen.
how: PostOnboardingStepType MANAGER_WELCOME, USAGE_MODE, AGENT_CONFIGURATION, ADD_WORKSPACE; CascadeNUXConfig {uid, location, trigger, priority, title, body, image/video url, interactions DISMISSED|ACCEPTED, requires_idle_cascade}; locations include model selector, plan mode, artifact view and toolbar; triggers include artifact created, project created, produced code diff, remote control eligible; SeenNuxUids persisted; telemetry events for each onboarding page; Skip for now.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has an onboarding feature directory but the chat page relies on cold-start suggestions (baseline s1); server-configured tips keyed by trigger and location can introduce Do mode, approvals and plan cards without releases.

name: Theming: light, dark, inherit and custom seed colours
what: Light, dark or inherit themes plus custom seed colours for background, primary and foreground overrides per mode, preset editor themes, and a selectable app icon.
how: ThemeMode DARK|LIGHT|INHERIT; CustomThemeSeeds {background, primary, foreground_override, primary_foreground_override} for light and dark; preset names such as Default, One, Tokyo Night, Solarized; Reset to preset; telemetry for selecting app icon variants (blueprint, classic, retro, sunset and others); VS Code token colour documentation strings are embedded.
verevonRelevance: Seed-colour theming (four colours generate the palette) is a light way to give enterprise tenants branded themes.

name: Settings information architecture with scopes and locks
what: Settings split into General, Chat, Agent, Browser, Customizations (skills, rules, MCP, hooks, custom agents, plugins), Permissions, Quota, Remote Control, Notifications and Experimental; per-project pages inherit the general values and show organisation locks.
how: UI section titles (Chat Settings, Workspace Settings, Experimental Features, Default Customizations, Personal Customizations, Custom Agents, MCP Servers); Inherit General vs custom mode; locked states with messages for strict mode, organisation management and unsupported builds; Reset overrides for custom feature flags in dev builds.
verevonRelevance: Verevon settings already cover memory, persona, skills, plugins and MCP (baseline s5, s8); a per-Space override with an inherit toggle and explicit lock reasons would complete it.

name: Home and empty states: quick start, project creation and suggestion chips
what: The home view offers New Project, Quick Start (instant scratch folder), workspace choice and suggestion chips that insert prefilled slash-command tokens (create an automation, create a plugin, review pending conversations).
how: CreateScratchProjectFolder RPC; project creation flows for folders and git; composer draft helper inserts markdown-link tokens of type slashCommand; Concierge welcome offers suggestion cards.
verevonRelevance: Verevon cold-start suggests from inbox cases (baseline s1); inserting a prefilled structured slash token rather than raw text keeps the prompt editable and typed.

name: Always-on voice Concierge agent (internal build)
what: A Concierge agent can listen continuously (toggle Ctrl+Shift+M, hold for push-to-talk); each spoken turn is sent to a dedicated Concierge conversation; a listener strip shows the state.
how: UI strings for concierge-listener-strip, voice mode active/stopped/failed, concierge_cascade_id; enable-concierge-agent flag; the agent binary path is Google-internal; voice recording is disabled while the Concierge mic is on.
verevonRelevance: An always-on listener conflicts with Verevon ZDR and the "no duplex voice" ruling (baseline s2); noted only as the direction competitors take.
notes: Appears gated to the internal appType; not available in the external hub.

name: Task-group presentation for long agent work
what: In planning mode the conversation groups work into task sections with an overview, list of edited files (click to inspect), collapsible subtask progress updates, and a dedicated section at the end listing steps that need approval so the user does not have to expand each one.
how: Docs describe the Task group layout; TaskBoundary steps and AccumulatedSection items (sections with title, icon, locations ABOVE_INPUT or SIDE_PANEL, max visible items) back the grouping; pending waiting_steps are summarised per trajectory.
verevonRelevance: Best-in-class answer to "what is the agent doing and what needs me": group by task, hoist pending approvals, keep detail collapsed; Verevon Work tab has the data (plan, todos, approvals) but not the grouping.
notes: Quality 5 from docs and data model; UI not exercised.

name: Responsive, accessible and performant UI details
what: Large lists are virtualised and paged, diff statistics are computed in a web worker, terminals announce limited output to screen readers, motion respects prefers-reduced-motion in some places, and the bundle has about 295 aria-labels; the UI copy is English only and the viewport disables pinch zoom.
how: index.html viewport maximum-scale=1.0; TanStack Virtual polyfill note; diff_worker.js; xterm accessibility strings; matchMedia reduced-motion checks in two components; no i18n library markers (no i18next or message-format calls) found; Chromium locale packs ship only for the Electron shell.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has screen-reader narration for runs and Norwegian/English (baseline s12); keep virtualization and a diff worker on the list, and avoid the zoom-blocking viewport.
notes: Absence of i18n and counts are from string search (medium confidence).

name: Process model: Electron shell, Go language server, loopback host bridge
what: A thin Electron shell starts a Go language server child process that runs the agent, serves the UI over loopback HTTPS and calls back into the shell through a token-protected local RPC (updates, window actions).
how: main.js launches languageServer.js with flags (--standalone, --subclient_type hub, --https_server_port, --csrf_token, --enable_sidecars, --host_bridge_url/--host_bridge_token) and detects the dynamic port from stdout; crash monitor restarts up to three times in 60 s; hostBridgeServer.js is a loopback Connect server with peer and Host-header checks and a 32-byte bearer token; headless mode skips windows; chrome-devtools-mcp and webm_encoder.exe are sibling helpers.
verevonRelevance: Verevon backend is cloud services; the transferable part is a loopback-only control channel with a bearer token for any local companion (Support Plane remote-core, a desktop runner).
notes: REA analyze_javascript_application on app.asar by the scout (61 IPC operations, 33 sender checks). Weak points: tokens passed as command-line arguments; Electron fuses at defaults.

name: Reactive state sync with ETag rows over Connect RPC
what: Settings and UI state (custom models, browser allowlist, planning mode, CDP port) live in topic/row stores with per-row ETags and applied-update acknowledgements, subscribed to by every window and remote client.
how: unified_state_sync proto (Topic{rows}, Row{value, e_tag}, AppliedUpdate{key,new_row,deleted,current_e_tag}, UpdateRequest); Subscribe/Push RPCs and Jetbox state subscriptions (JetboxWriteState, JetboxSubscribeToState, summaries); reactive component streams for cascade, panel and summaries; primitives with repeated and optional strings.
verevonRelevance: A small optimistic-concurrency state sync is a clean replacement for Verevon localStorage-based settings and pins (baseline s1, s12) and works across devices.

name: Protocol surface: one protobuf Connect service plus a public-shaped product API
what: The UI and all remote clients talk to a single large LanguageServerService (305 RPCs) plus services for plugins, remoting, index and extension bridge; a thinner product API v1 exposes conversations (create, list, get, update, delete) for outside callers.
how: language_server.proto 3,094 lines in the decoded descriptor; ExtensionServerService lets IDE extensions provide terminals, diagnostics, definitions and diffs; jetski.product.v1.ConversationService with RunState IDLE|RUNNING|CANCELLING; Remote Control tunnels these same RPC paths as ProxyRequestV2.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has typed action contracts and AG-UI that nobody consumes (baseline s5); a small versioned conversation API in front of session-core is more valuable than a giant internal RPC surface.
notes: The 305-RPC service (2,989 proto names overall) is a maintainability warning, not a model.

name: Brain directory: per-conversation files and transcript logs
what: Each conversation owns a directory holding artifacts, screenshots and a JSON-lines transcript that hooks and audit agents can read; knowledge items and sidecar data have their own directories under the app data dir.
how: Hook input includes transcriptPath and artifactDirectoryPath; embedded prompts refer to <appDataDir>/brain/<conversation-id>/.system_generated/logs/transcript.jsonl; sidecars get data, logs and events folders; configuration lives in config.json, mcp_config.json, hooks.json and skills folders under the user config dir; project store in JetboxAppState.
verevonRelevance: A transcript.jsonl plus artifact directory per run, handed to hooks and auditors, would give Verevon verifiable evidence outside the DB (compatible with proof bundles); keep it out of ZDR paths.
notes: Path template from an embedded prompt; the per-user directories themselves were not read.

name: Feature-provider UI with internal and external app variants in one bundle
what: The UI is composed from feature providers (agent team, concierge, side question, custom models, code search, file tree) and gated by an appType of internal or external, so Google-internal features ship as dead code in the public build.
how: The bootstrap code wires features conditionally (appType external enables the Electron-native feature; internal enables file tree, trajectory-source JETBOX and agent-team command); internal VCS (Piper, Fig, Cog, CitC, ABFS) strings remain in the shipped bundle and the language server.
verevonRelevance: Anti-pattern to avoid: ship customer builds with private features compiled out, not feature-flagged; it enlarges the surface and leaks internal names.
notes: Hygiene observation only; no private values recorded.

name: Update guard for running agents and bundled auto-update
what: Updates download in the background, install on quit or on demand, and the UI warns that updating cancels an in-progress conversation and lists active tasks before proceeding.
how: electron-updater channel latest-x64-win, first check 10 s after start then hourly; host bridge GetUpdateStatus/ApplyUpdate RPCs; UI Update Anyway dialog with active tasks and conversations; Restart to Update states.
verevonRelevance: Equivalent for Verevon is the graceful drain on redeploy (baseline: /readyz 503); the UX lesson is to show which runs are affected before a restart.

name: Cloud-assisted features and telemetry endpoints
what: Many capabilities depend on Google cloud services: model APIs, Code Assist quota and model lists, web search grounding, image generation, transcription, share links, marketplace and admin controls.
how: LS flags --api_server_url (Generative Language API) and --cloud_code_endpoint; ApiServerService RPCs (GetStreamingExternalChatCompletions, GetWebSearchResults, GetImageGeneration, GetTranscription, CreateTrajectoryShare, RecordCortex* telemetry); GetLoadCodeAssist, GetAvailableModels, RetrieveUserQuotaSummary in the LS.
verevonRelevance: Shows which agent features need a server (sharing, quota, transcription) vs run locally; for Verevon ZDR, any feature that uploads trajectories (share, telemetry) needs explicit propagation of the ZDR flag.

name: Deferred tool loading through a tool_search step
what: Instead of sending every tool schema up front, the agent can search for tools by name and load only the ones it needs; MCP tools can be lazily loaded and models can declare support for deferred tool loading.
how: TOOL_SEARCH step (CortexStepToolSearch {function_names, response}); McpToolConfig.enable_lazy_load and McpServerSpec.force_all_tools_eager; ModelFeatures.supports_deferred_tool_loading; tool_search tool in the binary; skills use a parallel skill_search tool.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane already has staged MCP disclosure (baseline gap 1 says discovery and staged disclosure work); a search-for-tools step keyed to a per-model capability flag is the clean way to scale tool catalogues.

name: Strict tool-argument validation and call timeouts
what: Tool calls can be validated strictly against their schema before execution and external function calls have a configurable timeout, with invalid JSON preserved on the step for diagnosis.
how: CascadeToolConfig.strict_argument_validation; CustomizationConfig.function_call_timeout_seconds; McpServerSpec.timeout_seconds and strict_argument_validation; ChatToolCall {arguments_json, invalid_json_str, invalid_json_err, original_arguments_json, original_name}; ToolOverrideConfig can rename tools or arguments, override descriptions and fix argument values.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane validates arguments and repairs MCP arguments with field-level errors (baseline s4); preserving the original and modified tool call on the step is useful for audit and replays.

name: Interaction timeouts for approval and question steps
what: Steps waiting for user interaction can time out after a configurable number of seconds and record that they timed out, so unattended runs do not hang forever.
how: CascadeToolConfig.user_interaction_timeout_seconds; CascadeUserInteraction.timed_out; CortexStepStatus WAITING; WaitToolConfig and a wait step for timed pauses; UI shows waiting-for-user-input and Needs Attention.
verevonRelevance: Durable approvals in Model Plane have no stated expiry for the waiting step (baseline s4); an explicit timeout with a recorded outcome would fit run watchers.

name: Model-initiated permission requests
what: Besides gated tools, the model can explicitly ask for a permission (or a custom permission resource) and receive the user decision, so the permission system works for actions that are not a known tool.
how: AskPermissionToolConfig and AskCustomPermissionToolConfig enable ask_permission and ask_custom_permission tools; PermissionInteractionSpec carries the resource, a reason, an action description and the trigger source; the user can persist a suggested pattern or edit the target before approving.
verevonRelevance: Lets a Verevon agent request an out-of-band capability (for example a new connector scope) through the same approval card instead of failing closed.

name: CLI execution modes: request-review, accept-edits and plan
what: In the command-line client the user cycles three execution modes with one key: pause for diff review before every write, auto-accept file edits, or read-only planning that outlines steps first; permission rules still govern shell commands in every mode.
how: Docs: default (request-review) shows a diff with accept, reject, full-screen and edit actions; accept-edits auto-approves read, create and replace tools and is inherited by subagents; plan prepends /plan and uses read-only tools; Shift+Tab cycles modes; legacy /planning and /fast commands were removed; /permissions sets request-review, always-proceed or strict.
verevonRelevance: A three-state mode switch (review each edit, auto-accept edits, plan-only) is a simpler mental model than separate toggles; Verevon Ask/Do plus plan_mode could map onto it.
notes: CLI-only per docs; the desktop app uses presets and review policies instead.

name: Headless CLI and OS-service daemon on the same engine
what: The same engine runs in a terminal client (agy), in a headless non-interactive mode for scripts and CI, and as an OS service (systemd user unit, LaunchAgent, scheduled task) that stays reachable through Remote Control.
how: Docs: agy -p for headless use; Remote Control daemon authenticates with CLI sign-in; shell Electron has a headless mode that starts the LS with --headless; trajectory sources CLI and SDK are first-class enum values.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane runs headless by nature; a thin CLI/daemon client over the same run API (with policy flags) is the cheapest route to CI and scheduled use.

name: One engine, many trajectory sources
what: Every run is tagged with its source (hub client, CLI, SDK, sub-agent, agent API, internal tools, evaluation or replay), so analytics, permissions and UI can treat them differently while sharing the same step model.
how: CortexTrajectorySource enum (CASCADE_CLIENT, INTERACTIVE_CASCADE, REPLAY, SDK, CLI, JETBOX, AGENT_API, SUBAGENT, EVAL, EVAL_TASK and async review/search sources); StartCascadeRequest.source; AgentMessageOrigin IDE, SDK_EXECUTABLE, SUBAGENT; the product API Conversation has RunState.
verevonRelevance: Add a source field to Verevon runs (chat, agent console, schedule, watcher, subagent, eval) so cost, quality and permission policies can slice by origin.

name: Status line and window-title scripts fed with live agent metadata
what: The terminal client pipes live metadata (directory, model, token usage, run state) into user scripts that render a custom status line and window title.
how: Docs list /statusline and /title commands and state that live agent metadata is piped into user shell scripts; related quota command /usage shows model quotas.
verevonRelevance: A cheap customisation and transparency hook: expose a read-only run-metadata feed (model, tokens, cost, state) that tenants can render in their own dashboards or terminals.
notes: Claude Code has an equivalent status-line script feature; the codex inventory also lists a status line.

name: Replay of recorded trajectories for evaluation
what: A recorded conversation can be replayed step by step against ground truth or loaded as a replay conversation, supporting regression evaluation of harness changes.
how: ReplayGroundTruthTrajectory and LoadReplayConversation RPCs; CORTEX_TRAJECTORY_SOURCE_REPLAY and EVAL sources; LLM_JUDGE trajectory type and section judge criteria with weights on prompt sections.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane trajectory recording is an in-memory ring buffer with Atropos export (baseline s4); persisted trajectories plus a replay RPC turn eval-lab-py cases into regression tests of real runs.
notes: Appears to be an internal engineering feature; not exposed in the hub UI.

name: Customization inventory showing where each item came from
what: A customization view lists every skill, rule, MCP server and agent with its origin (built-in, installed plugin, config, workspace, global) and an "everything else" bucket for items found in files outside plugins.
how: DiscoveryCategory BUILTIN, INSTALLED, GOOGLE3, CONFIG, WORKSPACE on WorkflowSpec and CortexMemory (discovered_in, discovery_category); UI labels Available globally, Loaded in workspace and Everything Else; Copy config file path and Open config actions.
verevonRelevance: When Verevon layers org, Space and personal instructions and skills, an origin label per item prevents "why is the agent doing this" confusion.

name: Workflows retired in favour of skills with agent-assisted migration
what: The older reusable-procedure workflows are being deprecated; the UI offers an agent that migrates a workflow into a skill.
how: WorkflowSpec message retains path, description, turbo flag and disable_model_invocation; UI notice plus Migrate with Agent; docs list a workflows-to-skills migration page and still list IDE workflows.
verevonRelevance: Lesson in extension-surface hygiene: collapse overlapping concepts (workflows, commands, skills) before a marketplace grows around them; Verevon should keep one unit (skills) and map slash commands to it.

name: Model aliases (Auto, Recommended) decouple picker from concrete model
what: Selections can be an alias such as Auto or Recommended that the server resolves to a concrete model and version, so defaults can be swapped without a client update.
how: ModelOrAlias {model | alias}; ModelAlias CASCADE_BASE, AUTO, RECOMMENDED (plus legacy names); DefaultOverrideModelConfig {model_or_alias, version_id} pushed by the server; UserSettings.last_selected_cascade_model_or_alias.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already pins intent modes (Budget, Balance, Genius) resolved server-side; a versioned default override lets inference-core roll a model change out to a cohort and attribute it.

name: Integrated terminals with agent hand-off
what: Users can open standalone terminals in the hub (xterm.js), send a selection to the agent with a shortcut, let the agent read terminal output, and validate a shell setup script that runs before every agent command.
how: CreateTerminal, ListTerminals, StreamTerminalOutput, SendTerminalInput, CloseTerminal RPCs; READ_TERMINAL step; keybinding terminal.sendSelectionToAgent (Ctrl+L); settings Enable Shell Integration and Command Setup Script with ValidateTerminalSetupScript; split terminals.
verevonRelevance: Only relevant if Verevon exposes a Space terminal view; the setup-script validation (dry run with a timeout) is a pattern for any per-user shell environment.

name: Manager surface: standalone quick conversations beside projects
what: The hub is positioned as a command centre for many agents: conversations live inside projects or as standalone quick conversations that run in an isolated scratch folder with their own settings and permissions.
how: Docs: Quick conversations and project conversations; sidebar sections Standalone Conversations and Pinned Conversations; CreateScratchProjectFolder RPC; Projects can be archived and have environments.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon general chat (no Space) versus Space-scoped threads; the explicit "standalone gets an isolated scratch workspace" rule is a clear tenant-isolation story.

name: Resume, rewind and fork commands in the terminal client
what: The terminal client lets users resume a past session (picker or --continue), rewind to a checkpoint (/rewind, alias /undo), and fork the conversation into another project; histories are scoped to the launch directory.
how: Docs: /resume (alias /switch), /rewind, /fork (alias /branch) copies the conversation up to the current turn but not the git checkout, agy --project and --new-project flags; the hub exposes the same engine through RevertToCascadeStep and ForkConversation.
verevonRelevance: Confirms the minimal rewind/fork command set (and that fork copies conversation, not files); good spec for Verevon thread-level checkpoints.
